what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission continued four notice-of-intent and request-for-determination hearings to December 15 because no DEP file numbers had been issued.
The Commission approved the Snow Riders' small town forest trail improvement proposal on a roll call vote.
Minor field changes at 36 Peninsula Drive and 141 Hemlock were approved, as was a certificate of compliance for 50 Page Street.
At 441, the applicant was asked for an engineer's letter on cutting back the roof and a plan to naturalize part of the lakefront; the septic stop-work order was lifted.
On the unauthorized tree cutting, the Commission allowed one remaining pine to be removed after a call to the administrator, with a replacement planting plan to follow.

why_it_matters: Projects on the lakefront and Peninsula Drive stay unapproved until DEP numbers arrive, so owners and neighbors wait through at least another meeting.
Enforcement at 441 and the tree cutting shows how the Commission handles work done outside a permit: remedies such as plantings and engineering review, decided case by case at open meetings.
watch_next: The December 15 meeting, where the continued hearings return and the 441 engineer's letter and shoreline plan are due; attendance for a quorum was raised.
The bylaw review committee request, which the chair said would go on a future agenda.

what_happened.line: The commission voted to send written notice that further silt reaching Page Pond from 615 Townsend Street will bring a daily fine until remediation is in place.
It tabled for two weeks the question of requiring a wetland specialist at 615 Townsend Street, pending legal review of the scope of work.
The 101 Pleasant Street subdivision and 41 Country Lane were each continued to December 1; 188 Whalen Road was also continued to December 1.
Negative determinations were voted for a Lancaster Ave garage, a Peninsula Drive screen porch (the addition was denied) and work at 37 Pearl.
The commission declined to use the town's right of first refusal on the Chapter 61A land on Holmen Street and will send the selectmen a letter saying so.

why_it_matters: The Townsend Street vote sets up a possible daily fine on a landowner and may bring legal costs to the town, which are paid from the town budget, mostly taxes.
Passing on the Holmen Street right of first refusal means the town did not move to buy that Chapter 61A land, a decision that rests with the selectmen's follow-up.
watch_next: The two-week return of the wetland-specialist question for 615 Townsend Street, after legal review of the scope of work.
The December 1 continued hearings for 41 Country Lane, 101 Pleasant Street and 188 Whalen Road, and the November 27 site walk.
